title: What If Earth Were 5% Closer to the Sun? The Oceans Would Leak Into Space

scenes.text: What if Earth sat five percent closer to the Sun? You wouldn't boil. Something slower would happen.
We orbit at one astronomical unit. Many models put the inner edge of the habitable zone at about 0.95, some as far out as 0.97 or 0.99.
At first it's just hotter. Models say the danger starts when the global average hits about 340 kelvin, 67 degrees Celsius, against 15 today.
Then the stratosphere gets wet. Water vapour that today stays low rises to the top of the atmosphere.
Up there, sunlight splits water into hydrogen and oxygen, and the hydrogen is light enough to escape to space.
Molecule by molecule, over hundreds of millions of years, the oceans leak away into space. That's the moist greenhouse, and Venus may be what's left when it ends.

description:
What if Earth orbited five percent closer to the Sun? Climate models put the inner edge of the Sun's habitable zone at roughly 0.95 to 0.99 astronomical units, so a small shift inward could push Earth into a moist greenhouse: once the global average temperature nears about 340 kelvin, the stratosphere becomes saturated with water vapour, sunlight splits the water and the hydrogen escapes to space.
Over geological time the oceans would be lost molecule by molecule, with a Venus-like runaway greenhouse the possible end state. Scientists note clouds could shift the boundary and that Earth has never been in this state.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The Sun is slowly brightening, so some models say Earth starts losing its oceans naturally in about a billion years. Where would you move the Earth? Drop your own what-if below.
